open_points.subject: prepare_request plain-HTTP instance-class validation
open_points.text: - prepare_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] A plain http base_url is allowed only when instance_class is in the imported PLAIN_HTTP_INSTANCE_CLASSES constant, an instance_class that is None or not a known class counting as the imported DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CLASS constant, or when the base_url host is a loopback IP address literal; any other plain http target gives plain_http_not_allowed; the host judged is always the base_url host, never a required Host header.
open_points.question: The requirement distinguishes known classes outside PLAIN_HTTP_INSTANCE_CLASSES from unknown classes, but no imported constant supplies the set of known classes; which passage must change, or how is whether an instance_class is known determined?

open_points.subject: prepare_request multipart file parts
open_points.text: - prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] For POST, PUT and PATCH without a file input the inputs not used in the path form one JSON object keyed by port name, sent as its RFC 8785 canonical bytes with content type application/json; with a file input the body is multipart/form-data with one part per input not used in the path in port name order, one part per file in list order for a many file port, each part having exactly the two headers Content-Disposition form-data with name set to the port, plus filename set to the port for a file part, and Content-Type, the port's media type for a file part and application/json without parameters for a value part whose content is the canonical JSON bytes.
open_points.other_text: - Port fields (exact, no others exist): name: str, direction: PortDirection, value_schema: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, cardinality: Cardinality, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass | None
open_points.question: A file port may have media_type None, but every file part must have a Content-Type equal to that media type and DescribedPart.media_type requires a string; must file ports be required to have a non-null media_type, or must the multipart rule define handling for None?
